kitDescription: Emma is a pure team healer whose entire kit is sustain. Her Skill 1 has a 5% chance, whenever she is attacked, to heal all allies for 10.77% of her final Max HP. Her Skill 2 passively raises all allies' incoming healing by 13.33% while she stays above 90% HP. Her Burst heals the whole team instantly for 39.6% of her final Max HP and additionally lets allies recover HP equal to 39.6% of the damage they deal over the following 5 seconds. She has no damage, buff, debuff, or weapon-modifying line anywhere in the kit, so her only relevance to the damage sim is that her heals fire teammates' on-recovery triggers.

redAssertions: 'DISCRIMINATES against the passive-heal mis-read' — RECON ARTIFACT: reads nonexistent 'heal'/'recovery' SimEvent kinds (engine emits none; log kinds are shot/damage/buffApply/buffRemove/reload/burstCast/fullBurstStart/fullBurstEnd), and its counterfactual patch writes ov.skill1.blocks on an ARRAY-shaped slot (silent no-op), so the assertion could never observe anything.
'recoveries occur, and every one of them is at or after a burst cast' — RECON ARTIFACT: same nonexistent event kinds → recoveryFrames is vacuously empty.
'the HoT emits MULTIPLE recovery events per burst, spread over ~5 sec' — RECON ARTIFACT: same nonexistent event kinds.
'the heal targets ALL allies, not just self' — RECON ARTIFACT: same nonexistent event kinds; no targetSlug/targetIdx exists on any emitted event.

'the burst is damage-inert' — RECON ARTIFACT: filters damage events by a nonexistent 'srcSlug' field (engine field is 'slug'), so the filter matched every unit; the 5 instances it caught are helm's. Emma's own burst damage is independently proven zero by the driver's E1 byte-equality pin and by the 9 passing totals assertions.

burst.kitLine: Recover HP equal to 39.6% of user's Max HP
burst.driverSaid: burstCast → allies → heal ticks:1; keyed to emma's OWN cast, not fullBurstEnter; magnitude recorded but unmodeled (no HP pool).
burst.blindSaid: S6: IMPLEMENTED identically (functionally identical override). S2b: load-bearing, burstCast not fullBurstEnter — driver matches.
burst.formulaCheck: A heal deals no damage; no bucket interaction. Event timing: burst-cast effects resolve pre-FB-window per the measured boundary rule — consistent. Recovery-event payload is the correct engine representation of a heal in a sim with no HP pool.
burst.explanation: Trigger identity is the load-bearing question and the driver nails it with a fixture where burstCast and fullBurstEnter diverge in BOTH directions (5 emma casts vs 4 FBs; 3 liter-led). Isolation test: HoT stripped → recovery firings == emma's burstCast count exactly. The fullBurstEnter counterfactual demonstrably produces a different volley set, so the pin discriminates. S2b's vacuity warning (emma might never cast beside liter) is addressed head-on by the calibrated anatomy and the non-vacuity gates.

burst.kitLine: Recover 39.6% of attack damage as HP, 5 sec
burst.driverSaid: burstCast → allies → heal ticks:5 intervalSec:1 (⚑3 cadence convention, marciana 'over 3 sec' precedent, recipe given); magnitude unmodeled and documented.
burst.blindSaid: S6: identical ticks:5/intervalSec:1 encoding with the same ⚑ and the same recipe (count a consumer's refresh popups across the window). S2b: FIX disposition — multi-tick across the 5s window, neither collapsed to 1 nor permanent — driver matches.
burst.formulaCheck: The tick count is the only measurable payload and it directly scales ally consumer refreshes; the ⚑ is the honest way to carry an unstated tick rate. Magnitude itself is out of scope per the magnitude rule (no HP pool exists to contradict the prose's number).
burst.explanation: Driver proves the cadence fires: exactly 6 recovery landings per emma cast through asuka's consumer (1 instant + 5 HoT), and the ticks:1 counterfactual collapses to 2 per cast — the assertion fails under its named nearest-wrong model. Two blind derivations independently chose the identical ticks:5/intervalSec:1 convention; the residual is the unmeasured tick count itself, which is flagged, not hidden.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas exist. The S5-vs-driver RED is entirely recon artifacts: all five failing assertions read SimEvent kinds ('heal'/'recovery') and fields ('srcSlug') that do not exist in the engine's event schema, and one counterfactual patch is a silent no-op on an array-shaped slot — these are blind-harness misreads of the engine, not divergences from the driver's encoding, and the 9 passing S5 assertions (including both stripped-skill totals-equality pins and the no-offensive-buff pin) independently confirm the driver's inertness claims. The substantive convergence is strong: S6's blind override is functionally identical to the driver's (same two burstCast→allies→heal blocks, same unmodeled sets), and S2b pre-registered every trap (fullBurstEnter keying, ticks-collapse, 'continuously'-as-HoT, interval-proxy for S1, dead-gate misread of S2) — the driver adopted and behaviorally pinned each one, including a fixture engineered so burstCast and fullBurstEnter genuinely diverge in both directions with non-vacuity gates. The driver's own 15/15 suite discriminates against each named nearest-wrong model (fullBurstEnter volley-set, ticks:1 collapse, heal-as-damage-buff), and the clean-weapon guard (27/27) plus E1 byte-equality prove her kit is damage-neutral. What must change for GO: nothing. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the ticks:5/intervalSec:1 lifesteal cadence is an unmeasured convention (flagged ⚑3 by both driver and blind, with the same recipe — a frame-read of a recovery consumer's refresh cadence across the 5s window) and is the only number in the kit that moves anything measurable; every other quantity is either kit-literal or documented as out-of-domain.
